computed at q_0 = 1.1099785955541805\ldots — the CODATA-2018 vintage of the muon pin, recovered by inverting CAL-2 at m_\mu/m_e = 206.7682830. The 2026-08-15 substrate fix that moved to the NIST table reached computations/ and tools/ and not content/. New pin q_0 = 1.10997859564273904668\ldots, from q-pinning-50-digit.witness.json; the shift is 8.0 \times 10^{-11} relative and nothing physical moves.

All seven rows, not the three a sweep found. An earlier pass substituted only the flagged figures and was reverted: the unflagged rows are q_0-derived too — they merely had some provenance, so the no-provenance sweep never saw them — and refreshing one column while its siblings stay behind leaves a table the reader cannot recompute from itself, which is worse than the stale value.

Three rows were also wrong at their own anchor, independently of the pin: 1 + q_0 (2.10997859556 against \ldots555), \log(1/\hbar_q) (\ldots982 against \ldots985) and \log(1 + q_0) (\ldots313 against \ldots315) — 1–3 \times 10^{-11}, neither the rounding nor the truncation of the retired value. Corrected here by construction.
